newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan raises '97 car export quota to EU by 13,000.
newsitem.headline: Japan raises '97 car export quota to EU by 13,000.

text.p: Japan and the European Union (EU) agreed on Wednesday to raise the 1997 quota for Japanese car exports to the EU by 13,000 vehicles over the 1996 quota, Japan's Kyodo news agency reported.
Officials with Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) were quoted by Kyodo as saying this year's quota would be 1.092 million vehicles.
The quota was raised based on a joint forecast by Japan and the EU that put overall EU demand at 13.916 million vehicles, up 193,000 from actual 1996 demand, MITI officials were quoted as saying.
Japan's 1996 auto exports to the EU reached 805,000, lower than the quota of 1.079 million vehicles set for the year, they said.
The quota was agreed through telephone conferences between Japan and the European Commission after the two sides failed to agree on a quota at talks in Brussels earlier this month.
Japan's 1997 export quota was 102,700 cars for France, up from 99,700 in 1996, 88,100 for Italy, up from 65,500, and 51,800 to Spain, up from 44,500.
Quotas were also set at 33,200 for Portugal, down from 34,000, and 179,900 for Britain, down from 180,000, MITI said.
The export quotas do not include cars assembled at Japanese automakers' plants in EU member nations, Kyodo said, adding that these will come under review later this year.
The voluntary export monitoring system, set up in 1993, will expire in 1999 after the full liberalisation of the EU auto market, the news agency said.
